original_target.title: Can one Dirichlet spectrum determine a Caputo potential?

verification: Literature and theorem-scope review; no independent whole-proof or Lean verification.

sources.scope: Exact Caputo realization, single-spectrum uniqueness expressly a conjecture after numerical reconstruction; Volterra normalization matches target.
Theoretical single Dirichlet spectrum uniqueness remains to be established.
Inverse theorem assumes eigenvalues together with norming constants for variable-order Caputo/RiemannLiouville mix; not one-spectrum target.
Apparent proven-uniqueness sentence traces to original explicit conjecture, not additional theorem.

registry_checks: No relevant Caputo alias in Palomar/Hexagon/OpenAI/Colbrook metadata; Palomar Caputo permanent inequality unrelated. Primary arXiv/publisher/author searches and Zenodo/HAL/GitHub focused queries.
scope_comparison: Must match leftCaputoorder1<alpha<2, additive arbitrary real boundedq and full complex zeros with multiplicities, no normingdata/symmetry. Two-sided or conformable derivatives, time-fractional evolution with classical spatial operator, convolution operators order>2 differ.
rationale: Bounded searches found no full matching resolution or announcement. A secondary thesis claim cannot override its cited primary paper's explicitly conjectural statement.
